steps.intent: Our objective is to keep the Council focused on an impartial OPCW investigation and to prevent any legitimization of unilateral military action, while preserving Syria’s sovereignty and avoiding attribution before facts are established. The main difficulty will be convincing the United States, United Kingdom and France not to veto language on restraint and non-use of force; we have therefore kept attribution out and avoided Chapter VII enforcement.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supports the Russian draft’s emphasis on Syria’s sovereignty, the OPCW investigation and restraint. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP5 by explicitly rejecting any unilateral military action against Syria and reaffirming that any response must go through the Security Council. This is essential to prevent escalation and preserve the Charter.
messages.China: China supports the Russian draft as a balanced basis. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP5 against unilateral military action and OP3 to make clear that the Council will await the OPCW report before further action. We also suggest adding 'objective' to the OP2 investigation criteria. These amendments are consistent with the Charter and help preserve Council unity.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d'Ivoire supports the Council's condemnation of chemical weapons and the role of the OPCW, but the text must clearly provide for accountability and immediate, unhindered access for the Fact-Finding Mission. We also believe the Council should directly condemn the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma while the investigation proceeds. With these amendments, Côte d'Ivoire can support the draft.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the Russian draft as a balanced basis for Council unity. We condemn any use of chemical weapons and call for a transparent OPCW investigation, while stressing Syria's sovereignty and the need to avoid escalation. We urge all members to support the text without divisive amendments.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the draft's focus on the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, sovereignty, restraint and a Syrian-led political process. We ask the penholder to make clear that all States must refrain from unilateral military action not authorized by the Council, and that the Council should await the OPCW findings before deciding any further response. Ethiopia can support the text with these amendments.
messages.France: France welcomes the draft's support for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission but cannot accept a text that treats chemical weapons use as merely 'alleged' or equates the perpetrator with the victims. We require explicit condemnation of the Douma attack and the responsibility of the Syrian regime, a mechanism to attribute responsibility, and deletion of the call on all Member States to exercise restraint. These are red lines for France; without them the text will not command our support.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports the Russian draft as a balanced basis for de-escalation and an independent OPCW investigation. We ask the penholder to make the non-use of force principle operational and to reaffirm that there is no military solution, so that the Council speaks clearly against further escalation. We are ready to support the text with these amendments.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait supports the Council’s condemnation of chemical weapons and the OPCW investigation, but the text as drafted does not go far enough on accountability. We ask that OP1 condemn in the strongest terms the reported use in Douma and stress that those responsible must be held accountable, and that OP2 explicitly require the Syrian authorities to provide full access and comply with resolution 2118 (2013). We also seek a new operative paragraph requesting options for an independent attribution mechanism and stronger humanitarian access language; these changes are essential for Kuwait’s support.
messages.Netherlands: We thank the Russian Federation for circulating this draft. The Netherlands can support a focused Council response that backs the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, but the text must be strengthened: it should condemn the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma in the strongest terms, demand immediate and unconditional OPCW access, and establish an independent attribution mechanism. We also ask that OP5 be narrowed to the parties to the conflict so that it does not blur the distinction between chemical weapons use and measures taken in response.
messages.Peru: Peru supports prompt Council action and an independent OPCW-led investigation into the Douma reports. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP1's condemnation and cooperation demand, to make OP3 report on access impediments and Council follow-up, and to add an accountability paragraph. We also suggest clarifying in OP5 that all responses must respect the Charter and Article 2(4).
messages.Poland: Poland cannot accept a text that treats the Douma chemical weapons attack as an unverified allegation and puts the perpetrator and the victim on the same footing. We need explicit condemnation of the attack, a mechanism to identify and hold those responsible accountable, and Chapter VII follow-up. We also cannot support language calling on all Member States to exercise restraint in a way that would constrain responses to chemical weapons use; these are red lines for our delegation.
messages.Sweden: Sweden can support the draft only if it clearly condemns the Douma attack and demands accountability, rather than merely noting alleged use. We also need OP2 to name the Syrian authorities and demand immediate OPCW access, and OP6 to include cross-border and cross-line humanitarian access and medical evacuations. We would further add language on women's full and equal participation in the political process.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: We cannot support this text as drafted: it fails to identify the Syrian regime’s responsibility for the Douma attack and its blanket call for restraint risks constraining a legitimate response to chemical weapons use. We need explicit attribution, immediate and unconditional OPCW access, a clear Chapter VII accountability mechanism, and deletion of language that could be read to preclude action under the Charter. We are ready to work urgently on a revised text, but these points are red lines for the United Kingdom.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft as written. It fails to attribute responsibility for the Douma attack, creates a false equivalence among parties, and its OP5 restraint language would constrain lawful responses to chemical weapons use. We require the red-line changes above—especially explicit attribution to the Syrian regime, a new investigative mechanism, and deletion of the restraint language—before this text can move forward.

steps.summary: This balanced revision aims to secure at least nine votes by strengthening condemnation, OPCW access, accountability and follow-up while avoiding explicit attribution or Chapter VII authorization. The Western permanent members are expected to abstain rather than veto given the strengthened condemnation and access provisions.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia supports the Russian Federation's effort to keep the Council focused on investigation and de-escalation. We appreciate the inclusion of Article 2(4), but given the public threats and reports of military action, OP7 should explicitly mention unilateral military action against Syria. Bolivia will support the text with this strengthening.
messages.China: China supports the revised draft as a balanced basis for Council action. It reflects the need for an objective OPCW investigation and for the Council to consider the OPCW report before any further measures, while reaffirming Syria’s sovereignty and the Charter principles on non-use of force. We see no need for further amendments and call on all members to support the text.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire supports the current text. We welcome the incorporation of strong condemnation, accountability, and immediate, full, safe and unhindered access for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission. We urge all Council members to unite behind this balanced text, which upholds Syrian sovereignty, demands compliance with resolution 2401, and supports a Syrian-led political process.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the revised draft as presented. It condemns any use of chemical weapons, demands full OPCW access, and insists that any further action be considered only after the OPCW reports, while reaffirming Syria's sovereignty and the Charter's non-use-of-force principles. We have no changes to request and encourage the Council to adopt the text by consensus.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia supports the Russian draft as a basis and welcomes the inclusion of OPCW reporting and Council consideration before further action. We continue to believe the text must more explicitly uphold Article 2(4) by ruling out unilateral military action not authorized by the Security Council. Please reflect this in OP6 and OP7; with that clarification Ethiopia can support the draft.
messages.France: France cannot support the current text as it stands: it condemns only a 'reported' attack and does not attribute responsibility to the Syrian regime, and it asks only for options rather than an investigative mechanism with an attribution mandate. The Council must condemn the Douma attack without qualification, clearly state that the Syrian regime bears responsibility, and establish or renew an independent mechanism able to attribute responsibility. France also continues to insist that any restraint language not constrain responses to chemical weapons use and that the resolution be adopted under Chapter VII.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan supports the current text. It reflects our key concerns: condemnation of chemical weapons, an independent OPCW investigation, respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the absence of a military solution. We appreciate the incorporation of the no-military-solution language and the Charter-based non-use-of-force formulation, and we will support the draft as it stands.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait supports the revised text and welcomes the incorporation of our priorities on accountability, OPCW access, and humanitarian access. We urge all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and to exercise restraint in order to avoid further escalation.
messages.Netherlands: The Netherlands welcomes the condemnation of the Douma attack and the demand for immediate OPCW access, but the Council must not be barred from taking further action while reports are considered. We therefore ask that the OP3 phrase 'before taking any further action' be removed and replaced as proposed. We also need OP5 to move beyond options and explicitly require terms of reference for a mechanism that can identify those responsible; with these changes we can support the draft.
messages.Peru: Peru supports the revised draft as a balanced basis and welcomes the inclusion of accountability, OPCW access reporting and Article 2(4). We ask that OP1 clearly condemn any use of chemical weapons while not prejudging the investigation, and that OP3 not freeze the Council's response by replacing 'before taking any further action' with language preserving the Council's ability to act as appropriate. We also support OP5 and would prefer a reference to the early establishment of an accountability mechanism.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot support the current text: it still refers only to a 'reported' attack and does not explicitly require the Syrian authorities to cooperate or establish an attribution mechanism. We need PP6 and OP1 to condemn the chemical weapons attack in Douma without qualification and OP5 to establish, not merely consider, an independent mechanism; we also continue to call for Chapter VII. Unless these points are addressed, Poland will not support the draft.
messages.Sweden: Sweden welcomes the inclusion of strong condemnation, immediate OPCW access, cross-border humanitarian access and women’s participation. We cannot accept a text that only asks for options on accountability: the Council must move toward an independent mechanism able to identify perpetrators. We also ask that OP3 not condition all further Council action on the OPCW report, which would weaken the Council’s ability to respond.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support this text as it stands. It still treats a chemical attack by the Syrian regime as merely 'reported' and rejects the Chapter VII attribution mechanism needed for accountability. We require explicit attribution to the regime, unconditional access, no clause deferring action pending an OPCW report, and a Chapter VII mechanism; absent these, we will oppose.
messages.United States of America: The current text still fails to attribute the Douma attack to the Syrian regime and would only ask for options on accountability rather than establishing an attribution mechanism. The United States cannot support a resolution that shields Assad and creates ambiguity about the right to respond to chemical weapons use. Unless OP1 names the Syrian regime, OP5 establishes a mechanism, and OP6/OP7 do not constrain self-defence, we will oppose.

replies.Ethiopia: accepted: OP6/OP7 reflect Article 2(4) and opposition to unauthorized unilateral action
replies.France: rejected: attribution to Syrian regime and Chapter VII mechanism prejudge OPCW investigation
replies.Netherlands: rejected: deleting report-first condition and premature mechanism unacceptable
replies.Peru: partially accepted: OP1/OP5 language incorporated; OP3 retains consideration before further action
replies.Poland: rejected: unequivocal attribution and Chapter VII mechanism prejudge investigation
replies.Sweden: rejected: attribution mechanism and removal of report-first condition unacceptable
replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: rejected: attribution to Syrian regime and Chapter VII mechanism unacceptable

steps.summary: The revision preserves Russian red lines: no attribution to the Syrian regime, no Chapter VII mechanism, and Council consideration of the OPCW report before further action. It is expected to attract nine positive votes but faces negative votes from several P5 members, so the draft would not be adopted.

reasons.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia’s anti-interventionist foreign policy and support for Syrian sovereignty align with the Russian draft, especially after its OP7 request was accepted. It would vote yes while condemning chemical weapons and demanding an OPCW investigation.
reasons.China: China supports the Russian draft, opposes unauthorized unilateral military action, and insists on an objective OPCW-led investigation without pre-judging responsibility. This aligns with China's established position and its recorded support in the last negotiation round, so the vote is Y.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire is closely aligned with France and Western partners but also supports chemical-weapons accountability; abstention avoids endorsing a Russian text that could constrain allied action and lacks a robust attribution mechanism, consistent with its historical vote.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supported the Russian draft in the last negotiation round and generally favors sovereignty, non-interference, and dialogue, making a yes vote likely; its low-key record suggests it would not take the floor to explain.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia prioritizes respect for sovereignty, the UN Charter and Article 2(4), and a multilateral OPCW-led investigation; its requested OP6/OP7 changes were reflected, so it supports the Russian draft.
reasons.France: France’s red lines—explicit attribution to the Syrian regime and a genuine independent investigative mechanism—were rejected, and the Russian draft would constrain responses to chemical weapons use; Paris therefore votes against.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan had already signaled support for the Russian draft; voting in favour aligns with its emphasis on UN Charter principles, non-use of force, OPCW accountability, and its generally cooperative stance toward Russia. The text calls for investigation and restraint without authorizing unilateral military action.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait’s negotiated position was support, and the draft condemns chemical weapons, demands OPCW access and accountability, and calls for restraint and a political solution, consistent with Kuwait’s balanced foreign policy. Voting yes also allows Kuwait to maintain Council engagement without endorsing unilateral military action.
reasons.Netherlands: The penholder rejected the Netherlands’ red-line change to OP3, leaving a report-first condition that would constrain further action on chemical weapons. The draft also contains provisions on unilateral action that the Netherlands cannot support in this context, so it votes against.
reasons.Peru: Peru’s key concerns on non-attribution before investigation and future Council action were substantially addressed; it can accept the sequencing in OP3. Supporting the draft also aligns with Peru’s emphasis on the UN Charter, sovereignty, restraint, and OPCW-led verification.
reasons.Poland: Poland’s red-line amendments on unequivocal condemnation and accountability were rejected. As a strongly pro-transatlantic, anti-impunity delegation, Poland would oppose a Russian text it saw as shielding the Syrian regime and constraining further action.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia authored the draft and it advances its policy: an OPCW-led investigation, opposition to unilateral Western strikes, and support for Syrian sovereignty. Voting in favour is certain, with a pre-vote statement to rally Council support and warn against military action.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden’s red-line request for an independent attribution mechanism was rejected, and the text would constrain follow-up action, so Sweden votes against in line with its accountability-focused policy on chemical weapons in Syria.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK already opposed the draft, and its red-line demands on attribution to the Syrian regime and a Chapter VII accountability mechanism were rejected. Voting against best reflects the UK's stated position that the Russian text obscures Assad's responsibility and constrains action to enforce the chemical weapons prohibition.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is committed to holding the Assad regime accountable and rejecting a Russian draft that lacks attribution and a credible standing investigation while constraining responses to chemical weapons use. This matches the U.S. red lines and its likely veto.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Mr. President, Bolivia condemns the use of chemical weapons by any party and under any circumstances. We support an independent, objective and transparent investigation by the OPCW and full, safe and unhindered access to the relevant sites. At the same time, Bolivia firmly rejects unilateral military action against Syria and reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, as well as the need to comply with the Charter of the United Nations and the principle of non-use of force. The draft before us includes these essential elements, including the amended paragraph 7, which clearly rejects unilateral military action. Bolivia therefore votes in favour of this draft resolution.
before.China: Mr President, China will vote in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. China firmly opposes the use of chemical weapons by any State, party or non-State actor. Any alleged use of chemical weapons must be investigated through a credible, objective, impartial and transparent process led by the OPCW, and conclusions must be based on reliable evidence. At this critical moment, all parties should exercise restraint and avoid any unilateral military action not authorized by the Security Council, which would violate the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations and the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria. The priority now is to de-escalate tensions, uphold the authority of the Council, and advance a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under United Nations auspices. China therefore supports this draft resolution.
before.Côte d’Ivoire: Thank you, Mr. President. Côte d’Ivoire condemns in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons, which is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. We support an independent, impartial and thorough investigation by the OPCW into the reports concerning Douma, and we call on all parties to cooperate fully and provide unimpeded access. At the same time, my delegation is concerned that the draft before us, while containing important elements, does not sufficiently ensure clear accountability and risks deepening divisions in the Council at this critical moment. For these reasons, Côte d’Ivoire will abstain on this draft. We urge the Council to unite around a balanced and effective response that upholds international law and the credibility of the OPCW.
before.Ethiopia: Ethiopia thanks the Russian Federation for reflecting important concerns regarding respect for the Charter of the United Nations, including Article 2(4). Ethiopia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We condemn any use of chemical weapons and call for a full, independent, objective and unimpeded OPCW investigation, with accountability for those responsible. At the same time, we stress that the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria must be respected, that any unilateral military action not authorized by the Security Council must be avoided, and that all parties should exercise restraint and return to an inclusive Syrian-led political process under United Nations auspices.
before.France: Mr. President, France condemns in the strongest terms the chemical weapons attack in Douma. The use of chemical weapons is a red line, and the Council cannot allow ambiguity about responsibility. The draft before us fails to name those responsible, fails to establish an independent mechanism mandated to identify perpetrators, and contains provisions whose effect would be to constrain the Council’s ability to respond to chemical weapons use. France cannot support this text and will vote against it. We remain committed to a Syrian-led political solution under resolution 2254, but accountability is not optional.
before.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan votes in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn any use of chemical weapons, and we support an independent, objective and impartial investigation by the OPCW with immediate, safe and unhindered access to all relevant sites. Kazakhstan has consistently upheld the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria, and the need to avoid any unilateral military action that could further escalate the situation. We call on all parties to exercise restraint, to cooperate fully with the OPCW, and to return to a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under United Nations auspices.
before.Kuwait: Kuwait will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and cannot be tolerated. We strongly support an independent, impartial and transparent investigation by the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, full and unimpeded access, and accountability for those responsible. At the same time, Kuwait underscores the need to respect the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Syria, to avoid any escalation, and to pursue a political solution under United Nations auspices in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015). The Council must speak with one voice and act in a manner that upholds the Charter.
before.Netherlands: Mr. President, the Netherlands condemns in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons. The reports from Douma demand a full, independent and impartial investigation, and those responsible must be held accountable. The Netherlands supports the demand for unfettered OPCW access and for compliance with resolution 2401. But we cannot support this draft, because it would condition further Council action on the OPCW report and would restrict the Council’s ability to respond to chemical-weapons use. Our requested changes were not accepted. The Netherlands will therefore vote against the draft.
before.Peru: Peru will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The use of chemical weapons is a serious violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security, and we condemn any such use. At the same time, attribution must be based on an independent and impartial investigation. The text requests the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission to report, demands full, safe and unhindered access, and preserves the possibility of further Council action. Peru also reiterates its commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and to a peaceful, Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under United Nations auspices, in accordance with resolutions 2254 and 2401. We call on all parties to exercise restraint and refrain from unilateral actions that would further escalate tensions.
before.Poland: Mr. President, Poland condemns in the strongest possible terms the chemical attack in Douma. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and cannot be left unanswered. We supported an unequivocal condemnation, full cooperation by the Syrian authorities, and a Chapter VII-based independent mechanism to identify and hold accountable those responsible. The draft before us does not meet these requirements; it weakens the response and fails to establish the accountability mechanism the Council needs. Poland will therefore vote against this draft.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution it has submitted. This text is balanced, objective and non-confrontational: it condemns any use of chemical weapons, demands full cooperation with the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, and envisages further Council action on the basis of a credible investigation. At the same time, it upholds the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and the Charter principle of non-use of force. We call on all members to support this draft and to refrain from any unilateral military action that would violate international law and further escalate the situation in the region.
before.Sweden: Sweden votes against the draft resolution. Sweden condemns in the strongest terms the chemical weapons attack in Douma and any use of chemical weapons. We fully support the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and demand immediate, full, safe and unhindered access for its investigators. But the Council’s credibility depends on accountability. This draft does not establish an independent and impartial mechanism to identify those responsible, and it would condition further Council action on consideration of the report. Those are red lines for Sweden. We remain ready to support a text that ensures independent attribution of responsibility, full respect for the Charter, unimpeded humanitarian access and a Syrian-led political process under United Nations auspices.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr President, the United Kingdom will vote against this draft. We condemn in the strongest terms the chemical weapons attack in Douma on 7 April. The pattern of behaviour, the repeated use of chemical weapons by the Syrian regime, and the regime’s obligations in territory under its control are clear. This draft is not a serious response to that attack. It fails to attribute responsibility to the Syrian regime, it equates the victim with the perpetrator, and it would constrain the Council and Member States from upholding the international prohibition on chemical weapons. It also seeks to make Council action conditional in a way that would provide cover for further delay and obstruction. The United Kingdom fully supports an independent, impartial investigation by the OPCW and accountability for those responsible. We cannot support a draft that instead protects those who use chemical weapons.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States cannot support this draft. The people of Douma deserve a credible, independent investigation that identifies who used chemical weapons, not a text that shields the Assad regime and its Russian backers from accountability. This draft fails to attribute responsibility, defers any meaningful mechanism, and includes language plainly intended to constrain the response to chemical weapons use. We regret that the Council is once again being asked to endorse a Russian proposal that would undermine, rather than uphold, the global prohibition on chemical weapons. If this text is put to a vote, the United States will vote against it.

after.Equatorial Guinea:
Mr. President,

Equatorial Guinea voted in favour of the draft resolution because it contained elements of fundamental importance to my delegation: the condemnation of any use of chemical weapons, the demand for a thorough, independent and objective OPCW investigation with full, safe and unhindered access, and the clear reaffirmation of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.

My delegation regrets that the Council has not been able to speak with one voice at this critical moment. We reiterate our strong condemnation of the reported chemical weapons attack in Douma and of any use of chemical weapons by any party. Those responsible must be held accountable through a credible and impartial process. At the same time, we stress that all parties must exercise restraint, avoid any unilateral military action not authorized by the Security Council, and respect the Charter of the United Nations and the principle of non-use of force.

Equatorial Guinea calls on all members to preserve Council unity and to support a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process under United Nations auspices, in accordance with resolutions 2254 and 2401. The humanitarian suffering of the Syrian people must not be compounded by further escalation. We remain ready to work with all Council members towards a balanced, credible and effective response.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation regrets that the draft resolution submitted by my delegation was not adopted. The text before the Council was balanced, objective and aimed at de-escalation. It condemned any use of chemical weapons, without prejudging the outcome of an independent investigation; it demanded full and unhindered access for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission; and it upheld the fundamental Charter principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity and the non-use of force.

We thank those delegations that supported the draft. We note with concern, however, that a number of members chose to oppose a text whose implementation would have helped restore unity in the Council and prevent further escalation. Their voting records today reveal that narrow geopolitical goals prevailed over the collective interest in an impartial investigation and a political settlement.

The Russian Federation rejects any use of chemical weapons and has consistently supported a credible, independent and objective international investigation. But we firmly oppose attempts to prejudge responsibility, to exploit the tragic events in Douma for political purposes, and especially to prepare unilateral military action against the Syrian Arab Republic. Any such action, taken without the authorization of the Security Council, would violate the Charter of the United Nations and international law and would carry the most serious consequences for regional and international peace and security.

We call once again on all members to exercise restraint, to refrain from any action that could further inflame the situation, and to return to the path of diplomacy and inclusive Syrian-led political talks under United Nations auspices. The Russian Federation will continue to insist on respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and on the central role of the Security Council in the maintenance of international peace and security.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr President, the United Kingdom voted against this draft because it was not a serious response to the chemical weapons attack in Douma. It failed to attribute responsibility, it sought to condition the Council’s future action, and it would have shielded those responsible from accountability. We regret that the Council has again been unable to speak with one voice on the use of chemical weapons. The United Kingdom reiterates its full support for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission and demands immediate, full, safe and unhindered access. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. Those responsible must be held accountable. The United Kingdom will continue to work with its partners to uphold the global prohibition against chemical weapons and to support a genuine Syrian-led political process under resolution 2254. We call on Russia to stop obstructing the Council’s response and to use its influence to ensure full cooperation with the OPCW.
after.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States voted against this draft because it was not a credible response to the chemical weapons attack in Douma. It failed to identify those responsible, it sought to constrain the Council’s ability to respond, and it would have given cover to the Assad regime and its Russian backers. The people of Douma deserve an independent, impartial investigation and real accountability, not a text designed to shield perpetrators. The United States will continue to support the OPCW’s work and will work with our allies and partners to ensure that the use of chemical weapons is not normalized and that those responsible face consequences. We call on Russia to stop obstructing the Council and to allow the truth to be established. Thank you.
